facts.statement: Eligible producers in Pontotoc County’s Local Administrative Area 2 have until Monday, Dec. 7, to vote for their representative on the Farm Service Agency county committee. A ballot delivered in person must reach the local FSA office by the close of business that day. A ballot sent by mail must carry a postmark dated Dec. 7 or earlier.
facts.evidence: The USDA map’s Pontotoc County office code 63214 returns three area records. Only Area 2 is marked with election year 2026. The dated notice distinguishes delivery from the mailed postmark.

paragraphs.text: Eligible producers in Pontotoc County’s Local Administrative Area 2 have until Monday, Dec. 7, to vote for their representative on the Farm Service Agency county committee. A ballot delivered in person must reach the local FSA office by the close of business that day. A ballot sent by mail must carry a postmark dated Dec. 7 or earlier.

The agency’s election map puts the U.S. Census Bureau’s reference points for Ecru, Sherman and Thaxton in Area 2. A town name alone does not tell a farmer which side of a boundary a particular address falls on. The USDA map lets readers enter an address or click the location of their farm to see the area. The county office can confirm it.

USDA mailed ballots in early November. Producers who live in the area and participate or cooperate in a USDA program can qualify to vote. A farmer who has given FSA information about an operation can count as a cooperating producer even without having received a program payment. Eligible voters who have yet to receive a ballot can ask the county office for one.

The person elected takes office Jan. 1, 2027, for a three-year term. County committee members help decide how federal farm programs operate locally, including conservation, commodity price support and disaster recovery.
